roleContext.title: What the mayor and council can do
roleContext.html:
The mayor chairs council meetings, speaks for council and has specific responsibilities for providing direction to the chief executive officer (CEO). The elected council votes on policy and budgets. The CEO manages day-to-day services and staff. Mayoral directions must stay within the Act and council’s decisions, including limits relating to staff appointments, discipline and unlawful conduct. Local Government Act, sections 12, 13, 104 and 170; Redland roles and responsibilities.

Who is involvedHow the mayoral role can help
Council services and facilitiesBuild support for policy, budgets, service improvements and decisions made by council.
State and federal governmentsBring people together, make submissions, seek funding and represent a council position that has been agreed.
Neighbouring councilsInvite shared learning, services, purchasing, mentoring or funding proposals. Each council decides its involvement.
Businesses and community organisationsListen to local needs and ideas, connect willing partners and support fair routes to grants, leases or contracts.
Luke’s projects and Strange But TruePut the public purpose first and use independent assessment and the applicable interest rules for any related transaction.

These options use a one-year planning horizon. The electoral term follows Queensland election law. Local government election guide.

roleContext.title: Public benefit and independent decisions
roleContext.html:
Writing an idea does not by itself settle a conflict-of-interest question. The actual decision and the officeholder’s financial and non-financial interests matter. Declaring an interest does not automatically allow someone to keep taking part in that decision. Local Government Act; registers of interests guidance.

The proposals begin with public purposes: lower avoidable costs, useful skills, reliable services, community connection and fair access. Council could compare ways to meet those purposes using clear criteria. A decision that could benefit Luke, Strange But True, his work or equipment, or an organisation he later establishes or joins would need the applicable interest process and independent advice before his participation.

Personal and Strange But True accounts and information would remain separate from council. General business support and a live tender have different rules. Council’s tender guidance explains the limits on contact with councillors. Any licence, donation, loan or use of Luke’s equipment would need clear terms and independent handling where interests arise. Council tender guidance.

Discussions would make clear whether Luke is speaking personally, for an organisation or on behalf of an agreed council position.

roleContext.title: Digital capability and council services
roleContext.html:
Personal AI, community learning, Verse Box, C-hours and public digital models connect with council’s responsibilities for services, information and privacy. The project introductions and names guide explain these terms. Council already has a Digital Transformation Portfolio, with existing systems, contracts and service responsibilities to take into account. Council’s digital program.

Joyful Responsible Abundance explains the wider goal: more people with the means to act and benefit. Preparing for possible superintelligence in 2027 or 2028 involves skills, privacy, reliable services, purchasing, access and partnerships. The timing is uncertain. The Sovereign Capacity Lab develops the related scenarios. Announced investment plans and money already spent remain different measures.

overlapGuide.title: Sovereign direction, compute, places and nodes
overlapGuide.explanation: Joyful Responsible Abundance supplies the whole-system direction for the Redlands sovereign-capacity proposal. Computing and hosting, shared civic places, and locally governed cultural intelligence nodes each have their own purpose. Power and material accounts, energy projects, manufacturing and repair provide distinct parts of the physical capability behind them.

overlapGuide.title: Council adoption, public simulations and personal data
overlapGuide.explanation: Council’s use of AI, simpler council interactions and public data simulations address different civic needs. Personal Aura concerns each person’s control of their intelligence and data; cultural intelligence nodes concern the authority of communities over their knowledge. Shared infrastructure would retain these separate permissions.

overlapGuide.title: Everyday skills, teaching, work and leadership
overlapGuide.explanation: Everyday AI and data learning, teacher development and Try Everything work experiences offer different ways to build skills. Women’s leadership and human mentoring extend those connections. Luke’s voluntary leadership practice concerns his own standards and conduct.

overlapGuide.title: Contribution, reciprocity and delivery organisations
overlapGuide.explanation: C-hours recognise voluntary contributions and their outcomes. Communities could choose the recognition and reciprocal opportunities they value. Ready Sustainable Employment and Training Cooperative (Ready SET Co-op) and GAJRA offer different organisational possibilities, while grant support and intergovernmental advocacy address applications, obligations, funding and policy.

overlapGuide.title: Genesis, public access, personal Aura and Geode
overlapGuide.explanation: Verse Box introduces creating a personal Aura through self-reflection and digital-twin patterning, with the aim of extending intelligence, learning faster and acting with greater intent towards Joyful Responsible Abundance. The optional adult Genesis/HBOT pathway adds healing intent and time-stamped biometrics for further pattern recognition, with an optional Truth Engine. Luke's chosen leadership standards, each person's control of their Aura and data, and the Geode equipment and experience work retain their own purposes.

overlapGuide.title: Everyday care, shared access and separate research paths
overlapGuide.explanation: Everyday support and carer coordination address daily continuity. Co-operative access concerns shared ownership and use of tools. Healthy-ageing, HBOT and longevity research, dementia software and carer-support research, and particular site partnerships each have their own responsibilities and research questions.

overlapGuide.title: Activities, neighbourhood venues and civic establishments
overlapGuide.explanation: Youth learning, collaborative escape rooms and creative participation are different activities. Neighbourhood venues, civic establishments and particular care, learning and research sites could host activities suited to their purpose. Several independent activities could use one place.

overlapGuide.title: Everyday publishing, resilient access and disaster coordination
overlapGuide.explanation: Everyday local publishing, resilient information access during disruption, and preparedness and recovery coordination have different roles. Shared content would retain clear publishing, equipment and operational responsibilities.

overlapGuide.title: Household savings, rules and council transactions
overlapGuide.explanation: Household bill checks address charges, offers and concessions. The legal information navigator explains applicable rules and routes to help; the body corporate navigator applies those capabilities to particular schemes. Council service improvements address completing and tracking council interactions.

overlapGuide.title: Food growing and sharing
overlapGuide.explanation: Dig for Redlands adapts Shared Table’s food-resilience and growing work for households and willing hosts across Redlands.

overlapGuide.title: Bee resilience and independent wildlife initiatives
overlapGuide.explanation: The locally led bee-resilience lab and independent wildlife and habitat initiatives each retain their own scope and participants.

overlapGuide.title: Reuse, workshops and manufacturing
overlapGuide.explanation: Tip Loop concerns recovering and redistributing useful goods. Makerspaces provide shared practical tools and learning. Manufacturing and independent repair concern productive capability and equipment continuity, supported by accounts of material requirements and reuse and recovery.

overlapGuide.title: Housing, road tunnels, island services and material reuse
overlapGuide.explanation: Temporary housing and servicing pathways, Minjerribah underground roads, utility alignments on individual Southern Moreton Bay Islands, and excavated-material reuse are separate proposals. The island-services proposal does not join the islands. Public information and simulations could help residents examine the different proposals.

overlapGuide.title: Transport, tourism, the Games and wider cooperation
overlapGuide.explanation: Independent ferry access and Gumpi scrutiny, tourism and domestic travel, and Games participation address distinct opportunities for Redlands. Reciprocal intergovernmental and international knowledge exchanges could connect wider experience, alongside any links developed through the GAJRA network.
